requestedChanges:
Request a REVISION of the current Sector Watchlist Cycle-3 specification through the normal LoopzAI specification-revision authority path.

Do NOT approve the current spec.

The core product design is good and should be preserved. This is a targeted revision, not a reopening of ideation and not a wholesale rewrite.

The main problem is that parts of the Verification contract violate our durable verification principle:

```
FREEZE THE PROMISE, NOT THE SNAPSHOT.
```

Historical/frozen tests must protect semantic behavior and required capabilities without permanently freezing incidental byte identity, exact file inventories, exact route sets, CSS implementation details, or historical commit snapshots unless those exact details are intentionally the product contract.

============================================================
REVISION 1 — REMOVE HISTORICAL BYTE-PIN CONTRACTS
=================================================

Current D11 / T-S1 / T-S2 / T-S3 freeze large parts of the repository
byte-identical to base commit:

```
dd823736d64116973b8169e0ddeb96519b194a9c
```

This is NOT an acceptable durable historical contract.

It would cause future legitimate changes to unrelated components/files to make
Cycle-3 verification fail even when the Manage Stocks feature remains correct.

Remove permanent/frozen assertions such as:

* `convex/**` must forever remain byte-identical to BASE
* `StockForm.tsx` must forever remain byte-identical
* `SectorCard.tsx` / `WatchlistBoard.tsx` must forever remain byte-identical
* Cycle-2 test/config files must forever remain byte-identical
* broad directories must forever match a historical commit

Replace them with the actual semantic promises of this cycle.

Examples of the intended durable contracts:

* Manage Stocks uses the existing stock edit/delete authority paths rather than
  introducing a second mutation path.
* Manage Stocks does not itself require a new Convex mutation/function or data
  model.
* Existing card Edit/Delete behavior continues to work.
* Existing Add Stock behavior continues to work.
* Shared/non-owner surfaces expose no Manage Stocks controls.
* The existing regression suite remains green.

If Verification needs to inspect the Cycle-3 execution diff to prove that this
particular implementation introduced no backend/data-model changes, that is
fine as CYCLE-SPECIFIC verification evidence.

Do not turn that implementation-diff check into a permanent historical test
that prevents legitimate future backend evolution.

Exactness may prove THIS cycle's change.
It must not accidentally freeze all future changes.

============================================================
REVISION 2 — REMOVE CLOSED-WORLD ROUTE INVENTORY
================================================

Current T-S4 effectively freezes the complete set of `app/**/page.tsx` files as:

* `app/page.tsx`
* `app/admin/page.tsx`
* `app/shared/[token]/page.tsx`

That is a closed-world snapshot.

The actual Cycle-3 promise is:

```
Manage Stocks is implemented as a modal and this cycle does not introduce
a Manage-Stocks route/page.
```

Preserve that semantic promise without asserting that LoopzAI may never add
another unrelated application route in a future cycle.

A future legitimate `app/settings/page.tsx`, for example, must not make an old
Cycle-3 test fail.

============================================================
REVISION 3 — NARROW ESCAPE BEHAVIOR TO THE APPROVED FEATURE
===========================================================

Current D10 expands `Escape` behavior beyond the Manage Stocks feature:

* existing Edit opened from a sector card
* existing Delete opened from a sector card
* existing Add Stock

all acquire new global Escape-to-close behavior.

That broader product change was NOT required by the frozen ideation.

Narrow the commitment.

Required behavior:

* When Manage Stocks is open, `Escape` closes exactly the topmost layer:

  1. Edit child if open
  2. Delete-confirm child if open
  3. otherwise Manage Stocks itself
* Closing a child returns to the still-open Manage Stocks modal.
* Escape must never accidentally close both layers.

Outside the Manage Stocks flow, preserve existing Add/Edit/Delete behavior for
this cycle.

Do not opportunistically add dashboard-wide Escape semantics.

If implementation cannot cleanly distinguish these contexts without modifying
the reused child components or introducing disproportionate complexity,
surface that as an explicit issue rather than silently broadening behavior.

============================================================
REVISION 4 — FREEZE MODAL BEHAVIOR, NOT MAGIC GEOMETRY
======================================================

Current D12/test design turns implementation/testing conveniences into product
contracts, including exact Tailwind-style geometry and reliance on viewport
coordinate `(4, 4)` being backdrop.

Replace this with semantic UI commitments:

* Manage Stocks renders as a modal overlay.
* It remains contained within the viewport with reasonable padding.
* Long stock lists scroll within the modal rather than overflowing the screen.
* The child Edit/Delete dialog visibly and interactively stacks above Manage
  Stocks.
* Clicking the Manage Stocks backdrop dismisses it when no child is active.
* Clicking a child backdrop dismisses only that child.

Prefer an explicit overlay/backdrop test hook if needed.

Do NOT make a particular Tailwind class, exact max width, exact 80% height, or
magic screen coordinate part of the durable frozen contract unless it is
actually user-facing product behavior.

============================================================
REVISION 5 — REDUCE DUPLICATIVE / OVER-SPECIFIED VERIFICATION
=============================================================

Review the 19 machine-scored + 5 human checks for redundancy.

Do NOT weaken meaningful coverage.

But simplify where several assertions prove the same promise repeatedly.

The verification plan should strongly prove:

* owner-only Manage Stocks surface
* correct ticker-sorted list and displayed fields
* Edit reuse + reactive update
* Delete reuse + reactive update
* empty state
* stacked-dialog/topmost dismissal behavior
* existing card controls remain functional
* Manage Stocks absent on shared/non-owner surfaces
* reasonable long-list behavior
* build/regression remains green

Avoid turning every implementation detail into its own permanent contract.

Verification should be proportional to this modest frontend feature and should
not become a second implementation of it.

============================================================
PRESERVE THE GOOD PARTS
=======================

Do NOT reopen or change the frozen product decisions unnecessarily.

Preserve:

* Manage Stocks is a modal, not a route
* owner-dashboard only
* Ticker · Name · Tags · Edit/Delete
* ticker ascending
* no search/sort/filter/pagination
* existing per-card controls remain
* reuse existing StockForm/delete path
* no count
* exact empty state `No stocks yet.`
* no empty-state CTA
* child dialogs remain stacked above Manage Stocks
* no new data model / mutation path
* no bulk actions or unrelated cleanup
* reactive updates
* human-verifiable acceptance behavior
* frontend-only intent for this cycle if implementation still supports it

Do not add the future "Simple Terms" human-summary feature during this project.
That is a separate future LoopzAI improvement.

============================================================
REVISION DELIVERABLE
====================

Produce a revised Cycle-3 specification that:

1. keeps the precise Execution contract,

2. remains self-contained for Verification,

3. implements the revisions above,

4. explicitly explains how the new test plan obeys:

   ```
   Freeze the promise, not the snapshot.
   ```

5. identifies any material product behavior that changed from the previous
   spec revision.

Then return to the normal SPEC APPROVAL gate and STOP.

Do NOT approve it automatically.
Do NOT begin Execution.

Wayne + ChatGPT will review the revised specification before approval.
